title: Active management graduation rule becomes risk-adjusted: an in-trade action class passes if it gives up <= a pre-stated R/trade (0.05R proposed) while cutting book max drawdown or worst-5% outcome materially (>=15%), across folds, vs a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book; then pre-register the break-even-stop-after-peak test on the real-money legs under it
note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-10-29 ~06:25Z (popup, verbatim answer): "Small R cost for big risk cut (Recommended)". Option text shown: 'Passes if it gives up at most a set amount of R per trade (I'd propose 0.05R, fixed before the run) while cutting the book's max drawdown or worst 5% of outcomes materially (e.g. 15%+). Must hold across time periods and beat a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book.' Operator reasoning, verbatim: "if we've gotten to a place where we can still find ourselves getting reward while zeroing out the risk of the trade, then that seems to me like it's a better trading decision overall than to keep on time and time again just giving back all of the gains." Supersedes the 'judged against hold' (mean net R) wording of docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md § Active management clause 4 for graduation. Unchanged: each class graduates on its OWN registered test; net of the full cost stack; rule registered before the run; Tier-3/mandate path to execute; two gates; TP doctrine. Motivating case: ADA-AM-CASE (break-even stop: EV cost 0.01-0.03R, worst -1.04R -> -0.17R, sub-floor n=19). [2026-10-29 ~06:35Z] OPERATOR, verbatim (generalises the rule into the system's objective): "This is an issue of metrics, not an issue of the trade itself ... If nothing else, reducing risk is always the second most important thing. So if everything else is even, then reducing risk is the right decision to make. And reducing lots of risk for a small cost in R is also the right decision to make ... the long-term P&L isn't just one trade. It's our ability to manage risk over time. And if we're not managing our risk because we're trying to get, you know, 0.5 more R or whatever, then we're obviously not going to make money in the long run." Reading: the objective is LEXICOGRAPHIC with a trade-off: (1) net P&L; (2) risk reduction as the tie-breaker; and a large risk cut for a small R cost is preferred. State it ONCE as the objective (ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL § Active management + OPERATING-PLAN § 2, or wherever the doc hierarchy says the objective lives) and point at it. [2026-10-29 ~06:40Z, Thursday planning] OPERATOR: "For the first one, yes, agree". Perf-review call D2 (giveback rise; pipeline PI-20261028-PVRNY2JI-0002) is folded into active management and graded under RULE-AM-RISK-ADJUSTED-V1, not a separate /perf-followup track. Disposition (a) for the planning close PR. [2026-10-29 ~07:10Z] OPERATOR, verbatim (sharpens the objective): "We've been measuring R, which is a good measure, and we need to continue that. But the main goal isn't most R as much as it's most overall P&L, right? We need to measure P&L and percentage on an absolute numbers because we're working with small accounts and different accounts of different sizes. But the what we care about is return, not necessarily just return for risk. We do care about R, which is why we also want to reduce risk when reducing risk will have a small impact on reward. But what we care about here is the overall amount of money that we make, not the overall amount of money we make necessarily in relation to the amount of risk that was taken." Reading: PRIMARY = absolute net P&L, reported in $ and % return per account (and book); R remains the per-trade unit of measure; risk reduction is the tie-breaker and wins when its reward cost is small; risk-adjusted ratios (Sharpe, return/DD) are NOT the objective. [2026-10-29 lane close] DELIVERED in one held PR. (1) Doctrine: ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL § Active management clause 4 now states RULE-AM-RISK-ADJUSTED-V1, with the operator's quotes. The system trading objective is stated ONCE there (06:35Z and 07:10Z quotes): absolute net P&L in $ and % return per account and book; R as the per-trade unit; risk reduction as the tie-breaker; ratios not the objective. OPERATING-PLAN § 2, the exit-refinement / live-trade-review / trading-desk skills, practice T13, programme 01, the desk-v1 plan and the MD-TRADE-DESK comment POINT at it (the parsed mandates are identical). (2) Grader scripts/research/am_risk_adjusted.py: a named, reusable rule over generic trade books, with explicit params. R1 is net P&L given up in R per trade, also reported as % return per account from accounts.yaml risk.risk_pct. Also exit_lever_ablation --grade risk_adjusted, and tests/test_am_risk_adjusted.py (positive and negative controls, end to end, harness-maxDD reproduction). Re-grade, a reading and not a graduation: comms/research/am_risk_adjusted/regrade-2026-10-29.json. NO class passes. The closest is break-even at peak 0.75/1.0R on trend_donchian_eth (ed1c-17): R gain, ~20% DD cut, 3/6 folds, no random control. (3) RQ-20261029-1f39-01 (break-even once peak >= 1.5/2.0/2.5R; the bybit_2 + alpaca_live rosters re-parsed at run time; pooled + per leg) is registered in research/queue/blocked/ with its rule, blocked on row HARNESS-BE-RANDOM-CONTROL.
